headers.comment: The SPA shell names the hashed chunks, so a cached copy pins the whole module graph to the build it came from. It was served revalidatable rather than uncacheable, and a route whose edge entry carried a Last-Modified older than the deploy answered revalidation with 304 — leaving a browser on a dead build no matter how often it refreshed, with the only symptom a failed dynamic import on the withdrawal screen. no-store removes the possibility: the shell is ~750 bytes and is fetched fresh every time.
Assets are content-hashed, so their URL changes whenever their bytes do. They can be cached forever, and should be — that is what makes an uncacheable shell cheap.
